name: Bass stomp box
subtitle: Homemade, Peterman-style · speaker run backwards · step-up transformer · passive

keyIdea.eli5: A speaker run backwards is a microphone. The box's own ring (about 80 to 120 Hz) is the tone control, and a transformer acts as a gearbox so a tiny coil can drive a long cable.
keyIdea.detail: No battery anywhere: all the energy comes from your heel.

summary: Heel hits the box. The box rings. The cone moves, the coil makes voltage, the transformer steps it up, and the amp makes it a kick drum.

top.label: (no power: fully passive)
top.eli5: There is no red rail here: this circuit has no battery. Your heel supplies all the energy.
top.detail: Passive means no power supply. That is why the transformer matters so much: it is the only way to make the signal 'bigger'.

bottom.label: 0 V (cable shield / ground)
bottom.eli5: The bottom line is the cable's shield: the return path and the 0 V reference.
bottom.detail: It carries no battery voltage, it just gives the signal a way home.

groundNote.eli5: Here ground is just the cable shield and the amp's input sleeve. There is no battery, so there is no + or − rail at all.

source.label: Peterman DIY stomp-box transducer (magnetic transducer + transformer)

notes: There's no published schematic. This is drawn from the description: a speaker as a generator into an 8 Ω to high-impedance transformer, no power.
Peterman's spare part ships as 'Transducer and Transformer'. It's a magnetic transducer, not a piezo.
Piezo contrast: a piezo is the opposite (very high impedance) and needs a buffer (a JFET preamp) or it sounds tinny.

honestyNote.eli5: A single chain is the honest picture here: this circuit really is one path from heel to amp.

job.eli5: A wooden drum: your heel's knock becomes a ringing low thump at the box's favorite note.

wire.eli5: Not a wire yet: the box's vibration, shaking the speaker cone.

job.eli5: A speaker run backwards is a microphone: the moving coil makes a tiny voltage.

wire.eli5: A tiny voltage from the speaker coil: weak, but able to push a lot of current.

job.eli5: Trades current for voltage, like a gearbox, so the weak coil can talk to a high-impedance amp input.

wire.eli5: The same thump at a much higher voltage, ready for a long cable.

job.eli5: A bass amp's input listens closely and the amp gives the thump its body.

wire.eli5: The thump at the amp's input.

job.eli5: The thing you stomp. It rings at its own low note, like a drum.
job.detail: Bigger box, lower ring. Its walls and the air inside both vibrate.

order.eli5: First: the box decides which notes even exist before anything electrical happens.

breaks.eli5: You'd be hitting the speaker directly: a click, not a thump.

job.eli5: A hand resting on a drum: it soaks up the ring so the thump stops sooner.

order.eli5: It acts on the box itself.

breaks.eli5: A long, boomy ring that can feed back at stage volume.

parts.label: Speaker (cone + coil + magnet)
parts.term: dynamic transducer (speaker used as a microphone)

job.eli5: A speaker run backwards: shake the cone and its coil makes electricity, like a bike dynamo.
job.detail: The box pushes the cone, the coil moves past the magnet, and a small voltage appears.

order.eli5: Mounted to the box, so it turns the box's motion into electricity.

breaks.eli5: Nothing turns motion into voltage, so there is no signal.

job.eli5: A gearbox for electricity: few turns in, many turns out, so the voltage goes up and the current goes down.
job.detail: That lets a speaker coil (low impedance: needs lots of current) drive an amp input (high impedance: wants voltage). Impedance means how hard a part resists a wiggling signal.

order.eli5: Right at the coil. The matching has to happen before the long cable.

breaks.eli5: The coil's tiny voltage goes straight to the amp: very quiet and thin.
breaks.detail: Wired backwards it gets even quieter.

job.detail: At kick-drum notes the cable's own capacitance barely matters.

job.eli5: The amp's ear. A high-impedance input listens without pulling on the signal.

order.eli5: The end of the passive chain.

breaks.eli5: A low-impedance input (mic or line) loads it down: quieter, and the bass shifts.

tune.higher: Bigger amp input impedance: the transformer's gearbox sees an easy load, so you keep level and highs.
tune.lower: Smaller: the amp drinks the signal, so it gets quieter and duller, like plugging a pickup into a headphone jack.
tune.tooFar: Below about 10k most of the stomp's tiny voltage is lost.

honesty.eli5: Modeled as a ringing filter (a resonator) hit by a knock. A real box has several ring notes and buzzes; the model has one.
Approximated as a fixed volume. A real speaker also filters what it picks up.

sections.title: Transformer
sections.eli5: Low voltage, lots of current in; high voltage out.

honesty.eli5: Approximated as a volume boost. A real transformer also rolls off the deepest lows and can saturate (squash) on hard stomps.
Modeled as a gentle treble cut.
